projects.name: National capacities supported and strengthened to effectively prevent, suppress and punish trafficking in persons in accordance with international standards and best practices, and to achieve sustainable impact through implementation of the National Action Plan against TiP
projects.description:
UNODC has been engaged with the Saudi Human Rights Commission (HRC), as chair entity of the National Committee to Combat Human Trafficking (NCCHT) since February 2020 in a multi-phased project of technical cooperation in the field of combating trafficking in persons (TiP). Therethrough, UNODC supports national efforts spearheaded by the HRC/NCCHT in preventing and combating TiP through a victim-centred approach that upholds the rights of trafficked and potential victims to protection, support, and care in line with international standards and norms and best practices.
Achievements under Phase I (February 2020 - August 2022) include the launch of the National Referral Mechanism (NRM) on 31 March 2020 which is currently managed by a central team in Riyadh together with 13 sub-teams in all regions across the Kingdom for effective coordination in dealing with TiP cases; the establishment of TiP specialized courts in all regions of the Kingdom with 124 prosecutors; the creation of the first-ever anti-TiP specialized Prosecution Unit on 30 July 2022; the creation of a specialized TiP Data Management Team; the development and adoption of the National Action Plan to Combat TiP (2021-2023); the legislative review and reform of the Kafala sponsorship system; and the delivery of 33 capacity-building activities that benefited over 1,600 officials within government entities, institutions, and CSOs.
Phase II (3 years, launched in March 2023) focuses on sustaining the outcomes of Phase I and further supporting the Kingdom through the implementation of the National Action Plan (NAP) against TiP. Activities include reviewing and updating the NRM; developing the electronic format of the NRM to support the availability, accuracy, and timeliness of TiP-related data; building monitoring and evaluation capacities for the implementation of the NAP; raising awareness of labour dispute committees, the media, the private sector and through religious authorities; conducting legislative and policy reviews; strengthening national capacities of law enforcement and criminal justice for the investigation, prosecution, and adjudication of TiP cases; supporting the creation of a national training resource/hub on preventing and combating TiP; and promoting the creation of partnerships for knowledge and best practices exchange.

The ultimate goal is to improve  NCCT capabilities to identify, assist, and protect victims of trafficking while reinforcing the overall national referral and response system in coordination with HRC and other government stakeholders.

projects.name: Advancing Human Capital Development in Tourism
projects.description: Since 2024, the Ministry of Tourism of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, in collaboration with UN Tourism, is strengthening human capital development through e-learning, workforce research, and education quality enhancement, ensuring a skilled and inclusive tourism workforce. A key initiative was the development of ten new Massive Open Online Courses (MOOCs), covering destination marketing, event management, digital transformation, and hospitality operations, and providing scholarships for Saudi residents, prioritizing accessibility, including for women. Addressing workforce challenges, the Tourism Labour Market Observatory (TLMO) is formulating a Comprehensive Labour Market Report and an AI Impact Analysis on Tourism Jobs, offering data-driven insights to shape policies that foster diversity and inclusion. Additionally, the UN Tourism.TedQual Certification is supporting Saudi institutions to align with global quality standards, reinforced by mentoring and quality assurance programs. The Tourism Faculty Development Programme (TFDP) further enhances curriculum design and modern teaching methodologies, equipping educators - particularly women - with advanced skills to lead in tourism education. Through these efforts, the Ministry of Tourism and UN Tourism are enhancing Saudi Arabia’s leadership role in tourism education and workforce development, fostering sustainable growth, innovation, and gender inclusivity in the sector. To support the tourism industry at the global level, the Ministry of Tourism of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia requested UN Tourism to make the MOOCs available in the UN Tourism Online Academy and that these are delivered in Arabic, English, Spanish, French, and Chinese.

projects.name: The municipal system is supported to be improved and restructured while updating settlements boundaries, revising municipal classification of Saudi human settlements and optimising service delivery
projects.description: This project is entitled: “Spatial Planning Reform and Visual Appeal Program in Saudi Arabia” is implemented by UNDP and UN-Habitat to support MOMAH. Over the course of four years, this initiative aims to enable systemic municipal and planning reforms and provide essential implementation and capacity-building support for the sustainable urbanization of Saudi cities. The project's overarching goal is to reinforce the Spatial Planning Reform and Visual Appeal Program in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This ambitious endeavor seeks to achieve six main outcomes, each designed to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of urban development and planning practices within the nation: 1. Delivering International Best Practices: The project aims to ensure that regional plans, local plans, and urban codes adhere to international best practices, setting a high standard for Saudi Arabia's urban development. 2. National Urban Policy: By developing a National Urban Policy to help govern and cascade urban governance and management at all levels, will help contribute to enhancing Saudi cities to develop sustainably and holistically. 3. Empowering Local Planning Departments: Through a new Operating Model for Planning Departments, the initiative empowers and enables local planning departments to better serve their communities. 4. Enhancing the Municipal System: The project seeks to improve and restructure the municipal system, updating settlement boundaries, revising classification, and optimizing service delivery for greater efficiency and sustainability. 5. Restructuring the Planning Framework: The Saudi planning framework will undergo a significant overhaul, with planning tools redefined, updated, and improved in alignment with new classification and categorization standards. Additionally, new tools will be introduced to support implementation and capacity-building efforts. 6. Upscaling the MOMAH Urban Design Studio: The existing MOMAH Urban Design Studio will evolve into a fully-fledged Urban Lab, equipped to spearhead innovative projects and serve as a hub for satellite labs supporting MOMAH’s mission.

projects.name: National Urban Policy for the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
projects.description:
The National Urban Policy (NUP) initiative provides a national framework to guide how cities and settlements grow and function. It brings together spatial planning, economic development, housing, infrastructure, and social inclusion into one coherent direction. The aim is to support balanced development across regions, improve quality of life, and align urban growth with national priorities and long-term sustainability goals.

The initiative focuses on clarifying roles and responsibilities across institutions, reducing fragmentation, and strengthening coordination between national, regional, and local levels. Through analysis, stakeholder engagement, and policy development, the NUP helps translate high-level national objectives into practical guidance for urban planning and decision-making. It also supports consistency across sectoral policies that affect cities, such as transport, housing, land management, and environmental protection.

A core part of the NUP is building an evidence base to understand urban trends, challenges, and gaps. This includes reviewing existing policies, assessing governance and legal frameworks, and identifying priority issues that affect cities and municipalities. The process emphasizes inclusive engagement, ensuring that public entities and relevant stakeholders contribute to shaping a shared vision for urban development.

Overall, the NUP serves as a strategic reference for future reforms, investments, and implementation tools. It does not replace existing plans or laws, but provides a common policy umbrella to guide them. By doing so, it supports more coordinated, efficient, and resilient urban development over time.

projects.name: Enhanced capacities to measure e-commerce and digital trade to empower digital economy policymaking
projects.description: The project aims to establish the evidence base needed to understand the current “state of play” regarding e-commerce in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (KSA) and provide a baseline against which to monitor future developments and the impact of policy actions. It consists of two tracks – a “domestic” track focusing on Saudi businesses as key actors in the e-commerce landscape with a view to assessing the degree of uptake of e-commerce and the value of business transactions facilitated by e-commerce in the Kingdom, and an “international track” supporting the development of internationally agreed guidelines and recommendations on measuring e commerce value through the UNCTAD Task Group on Measuring E-commerce Value (TG eCOM). The international track also includes the development of training materials based on those guidelines and recommendations, as well as the delivery of two regional training workshops to support their implementation across countries. The international track offers an opportunity for KSA to make the priority given to e-commerce measurement visible on the international stage and to cement a position among the leaders in this area, building upon previous initiatives such as the “Roadmap toward a common framework for measuring the digital economy” developed under the 2020 Saudi Arabian Presidency of the G20.

There is an urgent need to produce high-quality statistics to monitor, measure and evaluate national development plans and to report on progress towards the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals. The limited availability of data impedes advocacy efforts and opportunities for leveraging additional resources. As part of the new programme, UNICEF will forge closer partnerships with research, academic and policy institutions to build additional capacity on strengthening data for children. This includes reviewing the National Cooperative Strategy and the Executive Regulation of the Cooperative Law to align them with international labor standards and best practices. The ILO is also working to strengthen the Cooperative Societies Council (CSC), refining its role as an Apex organization to better support cooperatives across the Kingdom. To build technical expertise, the ILO is providing training programs for cooperatives, government officials, and educators, including a Training of Trainers (ToT) initiative and workshops on cooperative management. Additionally, efforts are being made to improve national statistics on cooperatives and increase awareness of innovative cooperative models worldwide through study tours, webinars, and multimedia content. These initiatives aim to create an enabling environment for cooperative growth, promote financial and organizational sustainability, and enhance the cooperative sector’s contribution to Saudi Arabia’s economic and social development.

projects.name: Build the capacity of Saudi youth though on-site UNV international assignments in selected countries
projects.description: MEP KSA signed an agreement with UNV offering 30 young Saudis international volunteer assignments for a duration of six months, which enhances exposure of Saudi nationals to critical areas of international cooperation and development while promoting the contributions of the Kingdom to achieve sustainable economic development around the world.  This programme will significantly in increasing KSA representation in the UN system. These UNV opportunities primarily focus on economic development and other priority areas as identified by the Ministry, with deployments take place in jointly agreed countries, namely Malysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Philippines, South Africa, and Oman.   The Project agreement was signed in June 2023, to start the implementation in 2024.

projects.name: Strengthen skills development systems and improve skills governance in KSA through assessment, capacity building activities, policy development and techncial support
projects.description: The ILO is supporting Saudi Arabia in strengthening its national skills development system by establishing effective sectoral and national skills governance mechanisms. This includes setting up National Sector Skills Councils (NSSCs) to align workforce skills with labor market demands, improving competency standards, and enhancing skills policy coordination. The initiative aims to bridge the gap between education and employment, ensuring a demand-driven approach to skills development that supports economic growth and job creation. Additionally, the ILO will provide strategic guidance for developing a national skills policy, institutional frameworks, and action plans while embedding expertise within the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) to drive sustainable implementation. Through these efforts, the ILO aims to enhance workforce competitiveness, productivity, and alignment with Saudi Arabia’s Vision 2030 goals.
projects.outcome: Increased knowledge and skills of population, especially women, girls and the most vulnerable groups, to enable them to participate in labor market, civic engagement and decision making

projects.name: Support improved policy development and implementation through placement of international advisers in the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development

These advisors will provide high-level technical expertise and on-the-job capacity building to support the development of national employment strategies, labor market analysis, skills policies, and impact assessment frameworks. Their role is to ensure that Saudi Arabia's labor policies and skills initiatives are data-driven, responsive to economic challenges, and aligned with international labor standards. This initiative reinforces the Ministry’s ability to address structural employment challenges, including youth employment and skills mismatches, while enhancing policy adaptation in times of crisis, such as post-pandemic recovery. Through this embedded advisory support, the ILO aims to strengthen Saudi Arabia’s workforce development and labor market governance in line with Vision 2030.

projects.name: Technical and capacity building support for effective functioning of the labour market information system in KSA
projects.description: The International Labour Organization (ILO) is working closely with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Development (MHRSD) in Saudi Arabia to strengthen and fully operationalize the Labour Market Information System (LMIS). This system provides up-to-date data and indicators essential for analyzing the labour market and monitoring and evaluating employment programmes. Additionally, the ILO is building the capacity of MHRSD staff by providing technical support and training on operating the system and analyzing data, enabling them to develop evidence-based policies. Activities include updating the system, training staff on managing and analyzing labour market data, and enhancing institutional capacities to ensure sustainability and effectiveness.

projects.name: Support to protect children, without discrimination, from all forms of violence, abuse, neglect and exploitation: (1) prevention and response services strengthened in targeted sectors, (2) knowledge and awareness on violence against children is increased

The programme will focus on strengthening government capacities to generate data to better analyse the causes and extent of violence against children, strengthen national response systems and monitor the effectiveness of national responses. The data will also be used to assist Governments to increase national awareness of child rights.

UNICEF and partners will facilitate the provision of technical assistance and access to high-level experts and international good practices appropriate for the Gulf. Technical and strategic support will strengthen the capacity of Governments to optimize existing child protection schemes. UNICEF will support government efforts to strengthen the capacity of families, parents and childcare providers to protect child rights and to identify, report and more effectively respond to violations of child rights.

Pedagogical materials will be developed and piloted through webinar series and materclasses to support the professionalization of young and emerging entrepreneurs working in the creative industries of AlUla. UNESCO’s experience in pioneering initiatives will complement the ongoing efforts by RCU, such as the ResiliArt Accelerator, as well as global frameworks such as the MONDIACULT Declaration (2022), ‘Cities, Culture and Creativity: Leveraging culture and creativity for sustainable urban development and inclusive growth’ (CCC Framework), and the ‘UNESCO Thematic Indicators for Culture in the 2030 Agenda’ (UNESCO Culture|2030 Indicators).

UNESCO is working in KSA on building capacities on preservation, digitalization and access to documentary heritage, building capacity on AI for civil servants and for judges, access to information trainings for civil servants and OER and IFAP program (IFAP Symposium and IFAP national commission) and MIL and AI literacy. 

On 16 August 2024, The Government of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia decided to present its candidature to the IFAP Council, at the elections to be held during the 43rd session of the General Conference of UNESCO in November 2025. UNESCO is currently in discussion with the KSA National Commission to organize a conference on the IFAP programme that will be followed by the establishment of a national committee for the IFAP. 

UNESCO is supporting KSA to improve its representation in the Memory of the World International Registry. Saudi Arabia has two inscriptions in the Memory of the World International Register:  Earliest Islamic (Kufic) inscription: The Inscription of Zuhair, 2003 and Arabian Chronicles in Stone: Jabal Ikmah, 2023 

Through the Royal Commission for AlUla, Saudi Arabia has committed to promoting documentary heritage from AlUla (ongoing) and Saudi Arabia in general through a contribution of USD 2,595,850 (2.59M) to the Memory of the World Programme of UNESCO.  The flagship activity under the AlUla MoW project i.e. Kingdom’s Institute Platform Conference for Innovating the Preservation of documentary heritage, was hosted in April 2025 at UNESCO HQ to create a stable dialogue mechanism open to the Arab region, which will act as a public sphere for discussion and presentation of best practices and novelties related to documentary heritage in the Arab world.

Additionally, the ILO is working with Saudi authorities to support the ratification of key international labor conventions related to social dialogue and tripartism. Through these efforts, the ILO seeks to create a more inclusive and participatory labor governance system, in line with international standards and Saudi Arabia’s broader labor market reforms.

projects.name: Regional Conference on Inclusive Tourism in the Middle East - Creating Accessible, Equitable, and Competitive Destinations
projects.description: The Regional Conference on Inclusive Tourism in the Middle East will be organised through UN Tourism’s Regional Office for the Middle East. The conference responds to Member States’ priorities of building more inclusive, equitable, and competitive tourism destinations, with a focus on accessible tourism, senior tourism, and women’s empowerment in tourism. It brings together government representatives, international organisations, the private sector, and civil society leaders to exchange experiences, identify challenges, and showcase policies and initiatives that advance inclusivity. The conference provides the Kingdom with visibility as a champion of accessibility and gender empowerment, while highlighting ongoing national efforts such as accessibility initiatives in Hajj and Umrah, transport systems, and hospitality services. This conference will also help the Kingdom to attract global attention and reinforce Saudi Arabia’s capacity to shape the inclusivity agenda in tourism. Moreover, with Saudi experts and institutions featured as speakers and moderators across multiple panels, the event supports domestic capacity building, strengthens collaboration with international partners, and enhances the Kingdom’s reputation as a forward-looking, socially responsible tourism destination.

projects.name: Workshop on Wellness Tourism
projects.description: Held at the UN Tourism Regional Office for the Middle East in Riyadh, the two-day event (9–10 September) brought together representatives from National Tourism Administrations and Organizations (NTAs/NTOs) from 12 Middle East Member States, with more than 30 participants in total, alongside industry experts and key stakeholders from across the region. Hosting the regional wellness tourism workshop in Riyadh strongly supported Saudi Arabia’s efforts under Vision 2030 by positioning the Kingdom as a leader in shaping innovative tourism segments. The event highlighted wellness as a core part of Saudi heritage and a defining element of its future tourism identity, while showcasing the country’s commitment to sustainability, inclusivity, and healthier lifestyles. By bringing together regional stakeholders and global experts, the workshop provided Saudi Arabia with valuable knowledge, market insights, and product development strategies that directly strengthen its capacity to diversify tourism offerings, attract high-value visitors, and reinforce Riyadh’s role as the regional hub for cooperation and knowledge exchange in the Middle East.

projects.name: Regional Digital Regulation Training Project for ITU Regions Supported by Saudi Arabia
projects.description:
The ITU Arab Regional Office partnered with the Communications Space & Technology Commission (CST) of Saudi Arabia since 2019 to support the dissemination of digital regulation trainings throughout the various ITU regions, while benefit the Digital Regulation capacity of Saudi Arabia as well. The project is being implemented in three phases of two years each. While the first phases ended in 2022, the first addendum added a third phase to the project that ended in 2024. Currently, the third addendum is being finalized and ready to sign with Saudi Arabia CST in order to implement a third phase for the project that will extend implementation to the end of 2026. The latest regional event supported by the project was a regional digital regulation training for Africa, that took part in 12-22 Nov 2024. The project has played a pivotal role in advancing digital regulation and transformation and strengthening national expertise in Saudi Arabia, which can be regarded currently as a Digital Regulator, especially after Saudi's creation of a National Digital Regulations Committee as part of the impact of this project on the Kingdom.

projects.name: Development and endorsement of walkability tools and measures in Al Ula
projects.description: The AlUla Walkable Neighbourhood Programme (AWNP), proposed by the Royal Commission for AlUla (RCU) and the French Agency for AlUla Development (AfAlUla) and supported by UN‑Habitat, aims to transform AlUla from a car‑oriented to a leading pedestrian‑friendly city. It focuses on delivering practical, operational outputs: review and refinement of a Walkability KPI framework and baseline assessments, a roadmap and implementation plan, a Complete Streets design manual, and a Walkable Neighbourhood Design & Policy Report. Alongside these technical outputs, UN‑Habitat will design and develop an AlUla Urban Lab as a strategic institutional platform to translate frameworks into policies and pilots, test innovations, coordinate cross‑sectoral stakeholders, and build local capacity and knowledge products for scaling.

projects.name: Establishment of the Tourism Law Observatory
projects.description: The establishment of the Tourism Law Observatory for the Middle East through the UN Tourism Regional Office in Riyadh represents a milestone in strengthening legal and institutional frameworks for tourism in the region. Building on the success of the first Observatory in Latin America and the Caribbean, this initiative provides a digital knowledge hub to collect, analyse, and disseminate tourism-related laws and regulations, while fostering dialogue among governments, experts, and academia. For Saudi Arabia, hosting the Observatory reinforces its leadership role in regulatory innovation and governance, in line with Vision 2030’s objective to create a competitive and transparent business environment that supports sustainable tourism growth. The initiative also enhances the Kingdom’s capacity to influence regional harmonisation of tourism law, attract investment through legal security, and position Riyadh as a centre of excellence and cooperation for tourism governance in the Middle East.

projects.name: Supporting the localization of SDGs in Saudi Arabia (Madinah and Qassim)
projects.description: As part of UN-Habitat's global mandate to support countries advance on the implementation of the SDGs at the local level, UN-Habitat has developed a comprehensive approach to enable local action in the UN system, by providing assistance through all stages of planning, policymaking, project development and monitoring. One of the five main components of SDG localization, includes support to cities in completing Voluntary Local Reviews (VLRs). In Saudi Arabia, UN-Habitat has supported Madinah and Buraydah (Al-Qassim) in undertaking and completing a VLR each. In Madinah, the technical assistance was geared towards supporting the Madinah Development Authority in reaching its SDG targets and adopting a people-centred urban planning approach towards becoming a dynamic, smart and sustainable city, delivering enriching experience for its communities and visitors. Next steps following the strategic plan and its impact will hopefully materialize during the course of 2025 and beyond. The VLR for Buraydah (Al-Qassim) was implemented in partnership with ESCWA with the view to support this authority enhance their existing approach to urban planning through evidence-based decision-making, leveraging high-quality data collection supported by the Qassim Urban Observatory. The Buraydah VLR focused on a structure approach to mainstreaming SDGs, promoting several stakeholder engagement activities and empowering local sustainable development aligned with national and global agendas. More than 60 indicators tracking the city’s performance were constructed, providing insights on the progress, limits and potential for 7 of the 17 SDGs – namely, SDG 1, 3, 4, 5, 6 11 and 17. The results aim to guide Buraydah urban development trajectory.

projects.name: Strengthening statistical data for industrial policy in Saudi Arabia

The project number is 230141 ( and not 182259). This project aims at supporting the institutional capacity of the National Industrial and Mining Information Center (NIIC) of the Ministry of Industry and Mining (MIM) in Saudi Arabia, in collecting and analysing statistical information for informing policy decisions in a timely and sustainable manner. This in light of the enhanced data needs to support the implementation of the National Industrial Strategy (NIS).
The project overall objective is to strengthen the availability and quality of manufacturing and mining data at National Industrial and Mining Information Center (NIIC) of the Ministry of Industry and Mining (MIM) in Saudi Arabia, to support the implementation and monitoring of the National Industrial Strategy (NIS) and related policies. It also seeks to enhance coordination within the national statistical system and promote the use of industrial performance indicators for policy guidance.

The lessons learnt will then be used to enhance the training, upgrade it, and upscale it nationwide.

projects.name: Developing a national model for trade and shock simulations (ATSI)
projects.description:
Upon receiving the technical assistance request from the Ministry of Economy and Planning in Saudi Arabia, ESCWA presented Economic Tools for trade analysis and the panel of Arab countries to simulate alternative national, regional and global trade policies and economic shocks on the national economy. During the various meetings organized at the ministry, other tools and potential developments were also presented and discussed including carbon tax on trade, and trade simulations at product level using modified versions of TASTE software.  The aim of the project is to introduce the major features of the existing interfaces and models and how they can be used by the Ministry for their daily work. The Ministry’s focal point expressed high interest to undertake a technical cooperation with ESCWA on developing tailored national versions of the GETSI and TASTI programs to timely assess the new trade agreements under negotiations between Saudi Arabia and its major trade partners in coordination with the rest of the GCC. The ministry expressed interest also to use GETSI To update its forecast for the kingdom and assess global changes on its economy. 
Capacity building workshops were thus organized:
1) Preparatory workshop in Saudi Arabia
2) training workshop on GETSI SA once finalized
3) Training workshop on linking GETSI-SA to simulation at products level using TASTE and GETSI

projects.name: Development of Makkah Region Authority
projects.description: ESCWA held an online coordination meeting with the Makkah Region Development Authority (MRDA) on 26 May 2025 to clarify needs and define the scope of support for the Makkah Urban Observatory. Following the meeting, MRDA shared three core indicator documents, enabling ESCWA’s urban development team to begin the technical review. The team conducted a comprehensive compatibility assessment between the Saudi indicator set and ESCWA’s Urban Monitoring Framework (UMF), introducing a refined compatibility scale and completing a full indicator-by-indicator mapping. The analysis also incorporated SDG linkages and visualized areas of alignment, synergies, and measurement gaps. These outputs were consolidated into a compatibility matrix, which ESCWA presented to MRDA on 29 September 2025.

projects.name: Technical support provided for the establishment of UNESCO designated sites (MAB program or Geoparks) for inclusive and integrated management approaches linking biodiversity conservation and sustainable socio-economic development.
projects.description:
KSA’s National Center for Wildlife acts as focal point for the UNESCO Man and the Biosphere Programme and has developed a management plan for the 2021–2023 period driven by the KSA’s aim to sustainably manage its natural resources and diversify its income generation away from the oil revenues by developing its emergent tourism sector. UNESCO is supporting the efforts of KSA through the organization of training, as well as through technical guidance.
In June 2022, Harrat Uwayrid was nominated as the second UNESCO Biosphere reserve in the country. KSA Natcom is heading the joint committee for MAB and Geoparks programs. KSA Natcom is also a member of the executive board of the ARABMAB network, headed by the UAE. To mark the International Day for Biosphere Reserves, 3rd November 2024, UNESCO, together with the National Center for Wildlife and Saudi Natcom, co-hosted the 1st Edition of the ARABMAB Youth Forum. 
Saudi Arabia submitted the nomination dossier for Imam Turki Bin Abdullah as the 3rd biosphere reserve in the kingdom. The MAB secretariat confirmed acceptance of the nomination dossier. The AlUla oasis also has great potential to join the UNESCO BR network. This is a subject that is currently at the heart of discussions between UNESCO and the Royal Commission AlUla (RCU), which has shown great interest in submitting a nomination dossier for the AlUla oasis as a UNESCO BR. In a strategic partnership being initiated between UNESCO and RCU, a global alliance will be launched to safeguard and sustainably develop oases worldwide. The proposed alliance aims to address these challenges by fostering international collaboration and sharing knowledge to protect, regenerate, and sustainably develop oases across the globe, capitalizing on the lessons learned from oases designated as UNESCO biosphere reserves. This alliance, led by AlUla Oasis, will create a platform for connecting oases worldwide, enabling them to benefit from collective expertise in heritage conservation, sustainable agriculture, water management, biodiversity preservation, and climate resilience.
UNESCO continues to promote the geopark concept in Saudi Arabia.  Two UNESCO Global Geoparks were designated in April 2025 by the UNESCO’s Executive Board: the Geological Park in Northern Riyadh, 120 kilometers from the capital, and the Salma Geological Park in Hail, northern Saudi Arabia.  
UNESCO, National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification (NCVC) and the Saudi Natcom organized a regional training on Geoparks program, in November 2024. NCVC expressed interest in hosting the second edition of the regional training to foster collaboration among Arab countries, exchange best practices and promote the concept of UNESCO Geoparks in the region.

Additionally, the ILO is enhancing the capacity of labour inspectors, law enforcers, and child protection officials to better detect, report, and prevent child labour. These efforts support Saudi Arabia’s broader commitment, as reflected in its G20 leadership, to eradicating child labour and ensuring safe, fair, and sustainable employment conditions for all.

projects.name: Relevant and effective learning outcomes, through increased supply of qualified and well-trained teachers, enhanced access to inclusive quality education and implementation of civic education
projects.description:
UNESCO plays a pivotal role in advancing the teaching profession globally, regionally, and nationally. In the Arab Region, UNESCO supports teacher policies, professional development, and inclusive education systems, working closely with Member States to address teacher shortages and improve quality education. Globally, UNESCO leads initiatives such as the International Task Force on Teachers for Education 2030, which promotes sustainable solutions to teacher challenges worldwide.
Saudi Arabia is an active member of the Teacher Task Force and has demonstrated strong commitment to global education efforts. Notably, the Kingdom supported the translation of UNESCO’s "Global Report on Teachers: Addressing Teacher shortages and transforming the Profession" into Arabic, facilitating broader regional engagement. The Arabic edition of the report was officially launched in Riyadh in May 2025, marking a significant milestone in regional collaboration for teacher development.

framework.name: Planet — Protect the planet from degradation, including through sustainable consumption and production, sustainably manage its natural resources, and take urgent action on climate change (SDGs 6, 12–15)
framework.description: The SDG/SDR 6 indicators that face major challenges are freshwater withdrawal, anthropogenic wastewater that receives treatment, and scarce water consumption embodied in imports. The SDG/SDR 12 indicator that faces major challenges is electronic waste. The SDG/SDR 13 indicators that face major challenges are CO₂ emissions from fossil fuel combustion and cement production and CO₂ emissions embodied in imports. The SDG/SDR 14 indicators that face major challenges are mean area protected in marine sites important to biodiversity and Ocean Health Index. The SDG/SDR 15 indicators that face major challenges are mean area protected in terrestrial sites important to biodiversity and mean area protected in freshwater sites important to biodiversity.

The SDG/SDR 9 indicators population using the internet, mobile broadband subscriptions, Logistics Performance Index: quality of trade and transport-related infrastructure, and Times Higher Education Universities Ranking: average score of top 3 universities have been achieved. The achievement of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. No SDG/SDR 11 indicators have been achieved as of 2021 as per available data. No SDG/SDR indicators that correspond to SDGs 7 or 8 face major challenges as of 2021. The SDG/SDR 9 indicator that faces major challenges is expenditure on research and development. The assessment of SDG/SDR 10 indicators is indeterminate due to a lack of data availability. The SDG/SDR 11 indicator that faces major challenges is annual mean concentration of particulate matter of less than 2.5 microns in diameter.
